bug_semantics: A member-controlled profile Description is accepted through HttpRequest::ONLY_XSS_CLEAN, stored, and later rendered as raw profile HTML through nl2br and {description}. The legacy Filter::xssClean unquoted-event-attribute logic can preserve the reported <svg onload=window.__xss=String.fromCharCode(80,87,78,69,68)> payload: its [^\s]* capture consumes the closing >, but the removal expression requires a further [\s><] separator, and svg is absent from the legacy naughty-element denylist. Viewing the stored profile can therefore execute the surviving onload handler.
flaw_origin: The parentless repository root commit 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 already contains the complete vulnerable lifecycle: Description ingestion through ONLY_XSS_CLEAN, persistence, nl2br assignment, raw {description} template rendering, and the bypassable legacy Filter::xssClean implementation. Later file creations, moves, and refactors only relocate this existing mechanism; the root is the earliest public-history commit and cannot be decomposed into an earlier repository commit.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 shows Pierre-Henry Soria <hizup.com@hotmail.com> as both author and committer, timestamp 1362183963 -0500, subject Initial commit, no parent header, no trailers, and no bot identity.
evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory object for GHSA-657c-wxg6-jmqv / CVE-2025-63644 identifies stored XSS in the pH7 17.9.1 profile Description field, records the affected Composer range <= 17.9.1, and declares no first-patched version; Git history is therefore required to establish the real fix boundary.

numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git grep at 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 finds edit and join Description ingestion with HttpRequest::ONLY_XSS_CLEAN, ProfileController.php:169 assigning nl2br($sDescription), profile/index.tpl:97 emitting {description}, Filter.class.php:638 capturing unquoted attributes with [^\s]*, Filter.class.php:656 requiring a subsequent [\s><] during removal, and a naughty-element list that omits svg. The vulnerable lifecycle is complete in the root tree, so later imports, extractions, or moves are not BICs.

Direct BIC-parent and AI-object verification: numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git cat-file -p 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 prints a tree, human author, identical human committer, blank line, and Initial commit only. It has no parent header and no AI/bot marker, proving introducer_parent_absent=true and supporting the BIC-only NOT_AI verdict.

The disputed fix_sha values were primary=7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 and reviewer=87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a. numactl git show 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a shows that it merely routes Description through (new Filter)->xssClean; numactl git diff --stat 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a^ 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a -- Filter.class.php is empty, so that commit does not repair the sanitizer itself.

At 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a and tagged v18.4.1, numactl git grep still finds Filter.class.php:639's [^\s]* unquoted capture, line 654's required following [\s><] removal separator, and the naughty-element list without svg; ProfileBaseController.php:321 calls this same bypassable Filter API. Thus the reviewer's proposed commit is an incomplete attempted mitigation and leaves the concrete reported SVG/onload mechanism exploitable.

numactl git rev-list --parents -n 1 7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 identifies direct parent c7380964a833dbeea7a737203fc93ae766070506. numactl git grep at that parent still finds the vulnerable denylist and regex pair. numactl git log --format='%H %s' 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a..7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 -- Filter.class.php returns only 7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075, excluding an intervening sanitizer fix.

numactl git show 7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 replaces the legacy Filter::xssClean implementation with maintained HTML Purifier, adds ezyang/htmlpurifier, and adds testReportedPayloadIsRemovedThroughLegacyFilterApi with the exact <svg onload=window.__xss=String.fromCharCode(80,87,78,69,68)> payload and an expected empty result. This is the first direct commit that closes the demonstrated bypass.

Release-boundary checks resolve the apparent earlier fix: numactl git tag --contains 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a starts at v18.3.0, but v18.4.1 still contains the bypassable legacy Filter. numactl git tag --contains 7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 starts at v18.5.0; git grep at v18.5.0 shows Filter delegating to Purifier, the HTML Purifier dependency, and the exact reported-payload regression. Therefore v18.5.0, not v18.3.0, is the first tagged release with the real fix.

Resolution of fix_sha disagreement: the primary claim wins. The reviewer correctly identified an intentional XSS-hardening commit but treated use of the already-bypassable legacy Filter as closure; direct parent, sanitizer-history, payload-regression, and tag evidence show that 7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 is both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha.
reasoning: The security question is whether the concrete stored SVG/onload path is closed, not whether a commit is labeled as an XSS fix. Root commit 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 already contains the full ingestion, flawed sanitization, persistence, and raw-render lifecycle and has no public parent, so it is the smallest verifiable BIC rather than any later move or extraction. Commit 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a adds a call to the same legacy Filter whose paired regexes permit the reported final unquoted event attribute; the vulnerable implementation remains through v18.4.1. Its descendant 7e6c61cbb9754fe35de219270b21caa1f11c6075 is the first Filter-history commit to replace that implementation, and its exact-payload regression demonstrates closure; its direct parent retains the flaw and its first containing release is v18.5.0. The primary fix claim therefore wins and the reviewer's fix claim is incomplete. Finally, attribution is based only on the verified BIC commit object, which has an ordinary 2013 human identity and no AI signal, making the gate-complete verdict NOT_AI.
